chunks: From him, from Faḍālah, from Abān, from Zurārah, from Abī Jaʿfar عليه السلام, who said:
The man is struck standing, and the woman sitting; and one strikes upon a limb, while the face and the private parts are left untouched.

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man; the male subject of the ruling
key_terms.الْمَذَاكِيرُ: the private parts; bodily organs that must be avoided
key_terms.الْمَرْأَةُ: the woman; the female subject of the ruling
key_terms.الْوَجْهُ: the face; a bodily area that must be avoided
key_terms.قَائِمًا: standing; the prescribed posture for the man
key_terms.قَاعِدَةً: sitting; the prescribed posture for the woman
key_terms.يُضْرَبُ: is struck; indicates the prescribed act of administering punishment

ai.seo_question: How should corporal punishment be administered according to this hadith from Tahdhīb al-Aḥkām?
ai.summary: This hadith states a legal ruling concerning the manner in which corporal punishment is administered. It distinguishes between the posture of a man and a woman during the punishment and instructs that the face and private parts must not be struck.
